rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans nearly the full organic range at a mid temperature, so all 10 compounds are likely to elute and we can map the overall retention window and identify whether the method is too steep or too slow.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is cutting t_last below 10 min. The first and last peaks correspond roughly to phi_e about 0.11 and 0.59, so a trimmed, steeper gradient centered on the observed elution window should keep all peaks in-gradient while shortening the run.

Resolution still has a wide safety margin, so push harder on speed by shortening the gradient and raising temperature to reduce retention, while nudging phi1 up slightly to ensure the last peak does not linger near the end of the gradient/hold.

The current method is fast enough, so the only way to improve CRF is to recover the one unresolved pair without letting t_last exceed 10 min. A modestly shallower gradient and slightly lower temperature should selectively reopen the 6/7 pair while likely keeping the last peak under the time threshold.

The 6/7 pair worsened when tG increased and T decreased, suggesting it is not helped by shallower slope and likely needs a different phi window/selectivity instead. Lowering phi0 while keeping the run fast shifts the gradient window earlier and changes the elution composition around the crowded middle region, which may reopen that pair while preserving t_last under 10 min.

The troublesome pair appears insensitive to gradient steepness but responsive to where in the phi window it elutes, so shift the whole window later rather than making it shallower. Raising both phi0 and phi1 together keeps the run fast while changing selectivity around the crowded middle peaks, giving a good chance to improve the 6/7 split without reintroducing a time penalty.

Shifting the phi window later improved the critical pair and also shortened the run, so continue that direction with the same gradient length and temperature. This probes whether the 6/7 pair keeps opening as its elution composition moves higher, while there is still ample margin on total analysis time.

At the later window, a new close 4/5 pair appeared, so keep the better phi window from injection 6 but make the gradient slightly shallower to lift both critical pairs together. There is enough time margin at t_last 6.5 min to spend 2 more minutes of gradient without risking a time penalty.

Changing the phi window helped more than changing slope, so now test temperature as the selectivity lever on the stubborn 6/7 pair while keeping the best window and fast gradient from injection 6. A small increase in T may reorder or separate that close pair, and there is plenty of margin to remain under 10 minutes.

Temperature clearly changes selectivity, and raising it to 55 C created a much worse 4/5 coelution, so go the other way from the best run and test 45 C at the same phi window and slope. This should reveal whether lower temperature opens the critical region enough to beat the current best without sacrificing the zero time penalty.

The best region is near 50 C, and the key sensitivity seems to be the gradient window rather than slope or temperature alone. Move phi0 later while holding phi1 at 0.75 to shift the crowded middle peaks to a slightly higher effective phi without pushing as far as the 0.20/0.80 window that created a new close 4/5 pair.

Injection 11 is the best so far and both limiting pairs are just below full credit, so a slightly shallower gradient at the same phi window and temperature is the most direct way to try to push them over 1.5. With t_last only 6.2 min, there is room to lengthen tG by 2 min and still remain comfortably under the 10 min penalty threshold.

Lengthening the gradient helped 4/5 but not the critical 6/7 pair, so the next lever is a slightly narrower, earlier upper phi limit at the current best slope and temperature. Lowering phi1 while keeping phi0 fixed should shift the crowded mid-eluting region to a lower effective solvent strength, which may improve 6/7 selectivity without threatening the sub-10-minute last peak.

Lowering phi1 made the 6/7 pair slightly worse, so test the opposite direction from the current best by keeping the successful later start at phi0 0.20 and adding a slightly higher upper bound at the same shallower slope. This should move the crowded mid-region to a higher effective phi, where earlier results suggested 6/7 improved, while the 10 min gradient may prevent 4/5 from becoming limiting.

The later gradient window continues to be best and the last peak is still comfortably before 10 min, so push the window slightly later again by increasing phi0 while keeping phi1 and tG at the current optimum. This targets the persistent 6/7 pair by changing the local elution composition without sacrificing run time.

Increasing phi0 too far collapsed the early peaks, so keep the successful phi0 at 0.20 and test a slightly higher phi1 than the current best. This preserves early-peak spacing while shifting the crowded middle region to a somewhat higher elution strength, which may improve the stubborn 6/7 pair without risking a time penalty.

The best score improved slightly as phi1 increased from 0.75 to 0.85 while keeping phi0 fixed, so continue that trend one more step. This tests whether the 6/7 pair continues to gain selectivity at higher effective elution strength, and there is still ample margin before any time penalty.

The best region is now clear at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.85, T 50, and the remaining score loss is dominated by the single 6/7 pair just below full credit. With t_last only 6.5 min, increasing tG to 12 min is the cleanest remaining move to buy resolution while still staying safely under the 10 min threshold.

Slope changes around the best window have not improved the stubborn 6/7 pair, so the remaining promising lever is temperature near the current optimum. Test 55 C at the best phi window and tG to see whether the altered selectivity can open 6/7 enough, while watching whether the 4/5 pair stays acceptable.

Temperature is clearly a strong selectivity lever at this window, and 55 C catastrophically collapsed 4/5, so test the opposite direction from the best method. This checks whether 45 C can improve the stubborn 6/7 pair enough to offset any loss elsewhere while keeping the proven optimal gradient window fixed.

The only unexplored corner near the best window is combining higher temperature with the steeper 8 min gradient, which previously gave better 6/7 behavior than 10–12 min at 50 C. This may move the selectivity enough to separate the persistent mid pair while the fast run leaves plenty of time margin if it works.

The robust optimum is around 50 C with phi0 0.20 and upper window 0.80–0.85; temperature changes are harmful, so use the remaining shots to finely tune the window/slope. This combination may keep the favorable 4/5 spacing seen at lower phi1 while giving a slightly different local slope than injection 14 to see if the persistent 6/7 pair can be nudged upward.

With only three shots left, the best strategy is local refinement around the top method. Shortening tG from the current best may improve the critical 6/7 pair slightly, as seen when steeper gradients sometimes helped that pair more than shallower ones, while still staying safely below the time limit.

One remaining useful check is whether the slight 4/5 weakness at higher phi windows can be countered by lowering phi1 while using the temperature shift that strongly affects this region. This specifically probes for a different selectivity balance near the current optimum neighborhood that might beat the best score if 4/5 improves more than 6/7 deteriorates.

The best region is clearly around T 50 and tG 10, and the strongest gains came from shifting the gradient window. For the last distinct shot, move the whole window slightly earlier than the best run while keeping a higher phi1, to test whether the balance between the 4/5 and 6/7 pairs can improve enough to edge past the current optimum.
